problems.stem: A capstone teaching plan has four labeled sections (scenario, prompts, adaptations, noticing) that never reference one another. Why does this fall short of an integrated plan?
options: It is missing a fifth section.
The parts are stapled together; an integrated plan shows how each move serves one teaching goal.
The sections are in the wrong order.
problems.explanation: Integration means the parts reinforce one objective. A collated set of disconnected sections is assembly, not a coherent plan.

problems.stem: A candidate submits a flawless capstone plan generated entirely by TeachGen@i, with no teacher edits shown. Why is this a problem for a teaching portfolio?
options: The plan is too detailed to be useful.
It shows no accepted, edited, or rejected AI input, so it does not document the candidate's own professional judgment.
AI plans are always lower quality than human ones.
The plan should have been longer.
problems.explanation: A capstone must record where the candidate accepted, edited, and rejected AI input. Undocumented AI authorship is not evidence of the candidate's judgment.

problems.stem: The capstone plan must cover a broad standard in one 40-minute period. The candidate cannot do both full coverage and deep practice. What is the defensible move?
options: Pretend the tension is not there and claim the plan does both.
Name the coverage-versus-depth tradeoff, choose depth on the highest-leverage subskill, and defend why with the standard and learner needs.
Let TeachGen@i decide and accept whatever it returns.
Cut the period short to avoid the choice.
problems.explanation: A professional plan surfaces the tradeoff and defends the call. Hiding the hard choice is not the same as resolving it.

problems.stem: Which Design Tension Studio map entry best captures an integrated, defensible capstone plan for a reviewer to audit?
options: "Combined all the module work into one document."

One objective stated, each module move (scenario constraints, constrained prompts, an access-preserving adaptation, a noticing-driven revision) tied back to that objective, plus a named coverage-versus-depth tradeoff with the defended choice and one rejected AI suggestion.
"Used AI to write the whole plan."
problems.explanation: The strongest capstone map shows one objective, integration of each module move toward it, a defended tradeoff, and documented AI judgment, all of which a reviewer can inspect.
